intro: Ordered from easiest to hardest. Start at the top, mark where you are, and note the frames you meet: they become the next drill.
tips: Read the French first. Look at the English column only after a paragraph you did not follow.
Look up only what blocks the plot. Guess the rest from context.
Note five frames a session (se mettre à, faute de, avoir soin de…). Copy them here and paste them into the chat.
Recognise the passé simple, never produce it. It is the narrative past of written French.

groups.title: B1: in this app
groups.note: Written to the course: only grammar you have covered, every hard word glossed, questions at the end.

items.title: Le dernier train
items.author: Le Carnet
items.blurb: A delayed night train, a father's old story, and a stranger who knew him. One passage, glossed, with questions.

items.title: La colocataire
items.author: Le Carnet
items.blurb: Two candidates for a spare room and a week of hesitation. One passage, glossed, with questions.

items.title: L'héritage, chapters I-V
items.author: Le Carnet
items.blurb: A notary's letter, an aunt's flat in Montmartre, a family secret from 1998. A serial, one chapter a day, about 500 words each, glossed, with questions.

groups.title: B1: for kids, modern French
groups.note: Written for French children today. The easiest real French there is.

items.title: 1jour1actu
items.author: Milan Presse
items.blurb: The news written for 8-12 year olds: short, current, modern vocabulary. A new article every day.

items.title: Vikidia
items.author: Vikidia contributors
items.blurb: The encyclopedia for 8-13 year olds. Pick any topic you like and read the introduction.

groups.title: B1+: kids' classics, free
groups.note: Nineteenth-century children's books. Simple stories, a little old-fashioned, free on Wikisource.

items.title: Mémoires d'un âne
items.author: Comtesse de Ségur
items.blurb: A donkey, Cadichon, tells his own life: clever, proud and often in trouble. Short chapters, plenty of dialogue.

items.title: Les Malheurs de Sophie
items.author: Comtesse de Ségur
items.blurb: A naughty little girl and one disaster per chapter: the doll, the bees, the goldfish.

items.title: Les Petites Filles modèles
items.author: Comtesse de Ségur
items.blurb: Two well-behaved sisters, and the unhappy girl who comes to live with them. The sequel to Sophie.

items.title: Sans famille
items.author: Hector Malot
items.blurb: An orphan sold to a travelling musician walks across France with a dog and a monkey. Long, gripping, in plain prose.
items.note: A novel. Read a chapter at a time.

groups.title: B2: short stories
groups.note: 2-4k words each, easiest first. Maupassant and Daudet, around 1870-1890.

items.title: L'héritage, chapters VI-X
items.author: Le Carnet
items.blurb: The second half of the serial: a lawyer, a biscuit tin of letters, and what the grandmother had planned. The bridge into B2.

items.title: La Parure
items.author: Guy de Maupassant
items.blurb: A borrowed necklace, a lost necklace, ten years of paying for it. The most famous twist in French short fiction.

items.title: L'aventure de Walter Schnaffs
items.author: Guy de Maupassant
items.blurb: A frightened Prussian soldier who wants nothing more than to be taken prisoner. Comic.

items.title: Une vendetta
items.author: Guy de Maupassant
items.blurb: A widow in Corsica and the patient revenge for her son. The shortest.

items.title: La Main
items.author: Guy de Maupassant
items.blurb: A judge tells the story of a severed hand that would not stay chained. Uncanny.

items.title: Le Père Milon
items.author: Guy de Maupassant
items.blurb: An old Norman farmer and the Prussian cavalrymen who go missing at night. War, peasant dialogue.

items.title: Le curé de Cucugnan
items.author: Alphonse Daudet
items.blurb: A village priest frightens his flock back to church with a tour of hell. A comic sermon, a few Provençal words.

items.title: La chèvre de M. Seguin
items.author: Alphonse Daudet
items.blurb: A goat who wants the mountain, told as a warning to a poet who wants to stay free. Lyrical, with Provençal words: the hardest of the short ones.

groups.title: B2: Arsène Lupin, gentleman-cambrioleur
groups.note: Nine stories of 5-14k words, Leblanc 1907. Side by side with the English, or French only.

items.title: L'arrestation d'Arsène Lupin
items.author: Maurice Leblanc
items.blurb: A transatlantic liner, a radio message: Lupin is on board. The first story, start here.

items.title: Arsène Lupin en prison
items.author: Maurice Leblanc
items.blurb: From his cell, Lupin announces he will rob a baron's château. And does.

items.title: L'évasion d'Arsène Lupin
items.author: Maurice Leblanc
items.blurb: Lupin tells the court he will not attend his own trial.

items.title: Le mystérieux voyageur
items.author: Maurice Leblanc
items.blurb: A train compartment, a robbery, and Lupin chasing the thief who took his place.

items.title: Le collier de la reine
items.author: Maurice Leblanc
items.blurb: A famous necklace vanishes from a locked room, and the answer goes back to Lupin's childhood.

items.title: Le sept de cœur
items.author: Maurice Leblanc
items.blurb: A night break-in, a stabbed card, a submarine's plans. The longest, told by Lupin's friend.

items.title: Le coffre-fort de Madame Imbert
items.author: Maurice Leblanc
items.blurb: Lupin is conned for once. The shortest Lupin.

items.title: La perle noire
items.author: Maurice Leblanc
items.blurb: A murdered countess, a missing pearl, and Lupin arriving one step too late.

items.title: Herlock Sholmès arrive trop tard
items.author: Maurice Leblanc
items.blurb: Lupin meets a very thinly disguised English detective.

groups.title: B2+: a novel
groups.note: One long book, read a chapter at a time.

items.title: Le Tour du monde en quatre-vingts jours
items.author: Jules Verne
items.blurb: A bet at a London club, eighty days, and a servant who keeps getting into trouble. Clear narration, a chapter at a time.

groups.title: B2+: Sherlock Holmes in French
groups.note: The Adventures, in a period French translation, side by side with the English.

items.title: L'Association des Hommes Roux
items.author: Arthur Conan Doyle, trad.
items.blurb: A pawnbroker paid to copy out an encyclopedia because of his red hair. Start here.

items.title: La Bande Mouchetée
items.author: Arthur Conan Doyle, trad.
items.blurb: A woman afraid of dying the way her sister did, in a locked room. The best known.

items.title: Un Scandale en Bohème
items.author: Arthur Conan Doyle, trad.
items.blurb: A king, a compromising photograph, and the woman who outwits Holmes.

items.title: Une Affaire d'Identité
items.author: Arthur Conan Doyle, trad.
items.blurb: A fiancé who vanishes on the wedding morning.

items.title: Le Mystère de la Vallée de Boscombe
items.author: Arthur Conan Doyle, trad.
items.blurb: A son accused of killing his father by a pool.

items.title: Les Cinq Pépins d'Orange
items.author: Arthur Conan Doyle, trad.
items.blurb: Five orange pips in an envelope, and men who die after receiving them.

items.title: L'Homme à la Lèvre Retroussée
items.author: Arthur Conan Doyle, trad.
items.blurb: A respectable man seen at the window of an opium den.

items.title: L'Escarboucle Bleue
items.author: Arthur Conan Doyle, trad.
items.blurb: A stolen jewel found inside a Christmas goose.

items.title: Le Pouce de l'Ingénieur
items.author: Arthur Conan Doyle, trad.
items.blurb: An engineer hired at night who comes back without his thumb.

items.title: Le Gentilhomme Célibataire
items.author: Arthur Conan Doyle, trad.
items.blurb: A bride who disappears from her own wedding breakfast.

items.title: Le Diadème de Béryls
items.author: Arthur Conan Doyle, trad.
items.blurb: A banker's son caught holding a damaged crown.

items.title: Les Hêtres Pourpres
items.author: Arthur Conan Doyle, trad.
items.blurb: A governess paid too much to cut her hair and sit by a window.
